relatedSnapshot.title: Cold email agent: capture, persist & reuse podcast name (wizard step + generate-and-confirm + settings)
relatedSnapshot.description:
PR 2 of 2. **Blocked by** ENG-10571 (the prompt must already consume `podcastName`). Plan: `/Users/jmske/.claude/plans/let-s-create-a-plan-tender-yeti.md` (§2.x + H9-H14).

## Problem

Proven podcast copy needs a real, credible show name, but there's nowhere to capture, store, or reuse one. Asking every campaign is friction; generic "the podcast" underperforms.

## Solution

Persist one podcast name per workspace, ask/generate it once, reuse everywhere, editable. Never hard-block.

1. **Migration:** nullable `podcastName: text('podcast_name')` on `aiSdrSettingTable` (`lib/db/schema/ai-sdr.ts` ~:53). `bun db:generate`; single ADD COLUMN, no rename; must apply before app serves (H13).
2. **Settings tRPC** (`trpc/routers/ai-sdr.ts`): `getSettings` returns `podcastName ?? null` (~:289). New `updatePodcastName` as `mutationRestrictedProcedure` (match :301) **+ org-membership/write check (H9)**; normalize `trim()`, blank→`null`; upsert ONLY `podcast_name` (no full-settings clobber — confirm `updateSettings.set()` excludes it, H10).
3. **Thread** `podcastName` **through the allowlist chain (each hop):** `CreateCampaignInput` + campaign schemas (`lib/outreach/schemas/campaigns.ts`) → `createOrUpdateCampaign` mutation (`trpc/routers/outreach/campaigns.ts:~1655`) → `parseCampaignCreationRequirements inputData` **allowlist (**`lib/services/util.ts:102` **— silent-drop choke point)** → service (`lib/services/campaign-creator.ts:102`) → `campaignCreatorInputSchema` (`lib/inngest/functions/campaign/types.ts`) → `processCampaignCreator` (`:~128`, destructure + fallback to stored setting). Also add to standalone `coldEmailPodcastSchema` (`schemas/submissions/cold-email-writer.ts:28`).
4. **Standalone form (DUPLICATED schema):** add `podcastName` to the local `podcastSchema` (`components/acquisition/cold-email-writer-form.tsx:58`); optional "Name 1 name" input on the podcast branch, pre-filled from `aiSdr.getSettings()`, with a "Generate for me" button; persist via `updatePodcastName` (H11: save failure → toast but still pass entered name; non-blocking submit).
5. **Wizard substep (BOTH generation entry points):** add `PodcastName` to `SequenceSubStep` (`types/campaign.ts:832`) + `podcastName`/`setPodcastName` state (`hooks/campaign/use-campaign-wizard.ts`); route to it when `method===Name 1` AND stored `podcastName?.trim()` empty, in **both** `handleEmailMethodNext` (`campaign-wizard.tsx:328,352`) AND the CSV/simple-targeting path (`:471`→onCreateCampaign `:499`); render branch alongside `:709/:719`; back→method/targeting, next→input or Generate→confirm→`updatePodcastName`→continue. New step component in `components/campaigns/new/steps/`.
6. **Generate-and-confirm + auto-persist (§2.8, H12):** `generatePodcastName({ targetIndustry, niche, researchBrief? })` (small Sonnet call → `{ name }`, ChatGPT naming rules: 2-4 words, credible, niche-fit, no em-dash); tRPC `aiSdr.generatePodcastName` powers the Generate buttons. In `processCampaignCreator`, when no name in event/settings → generate, **persist to** `ai_sdr_setting.podcast_name` **(first-write-wins, race-guarded)**, log secret-safe, use it.

## Scope

**In:** podcast-name capture/persist/reuse/edit across wizard + standalone form + automated paths; generate-and-confirm.
**Out:** generation/prompt/model changes (ENG-10571); onboarding (its duplicated schemas at `lib/inngest/functions/onboarding/cold-email.ts:41,81` stay generic, untouched — add a compile/regression test); hard-blocking any path; interview (uses a generated study title, no stored name).

## Saved model / behavior

Single source of truth: `ai_sdr_setting.podcast_name` (org-level, nullable). Blank stored as `null`. Wizard skip logic checks `podcastName?.trim()`. Partial write only (never clobbers other AI SDR settings). Automated/no-UI paths auto-generate once and persist (first-write-wins) → consistent across the org's campaigns, editable later.

## Permissions / ownership

`updatePodcastName` + `generatePodcastName`: `mutationRestrictedProcedure`, caller must belong to `organizationId` with write permission. Org-scoped read in `getSettings`.

## UX behavior

* Wizard podcast path with no saved name → a "Name 1 name" substep (text input + "Generate for me" → confirm/edit). If a name exists → skipped silently.
* Standalone podcast form → optional "Name 1 name" field pre-filled from the saved value, with a Generate button; edits persist for reuse.
* Name is reused on every subsequent podcast campaign; never asked twice.
* Spin/name visible in campaign sequence editor as the saved value (not a merge tag).

## Acceptance criteria

* New podcast campaign with empty saved name → substep appears via **both** wizard entry points; saving/generating persists org-level; next campaign skips the step.
* Standalone form pre-fills from saved value and persists edits without clobbering other AI SDR settings.
* `parseCampaignCreationRequirements` carries `podcastName` end-to-end into the prompt.
* Automated path with no name auto-generates + persists once; reused thereafter.
* Blank input stored as `null`; `getSettings` returns `null`.
* `updatePodcastName`/`generatePodcastName` reject callers outside the org.
* Onboarding caller compiles + runs unchanged.

## Open design follow-ups

* Should the wizard "Generate for me" reuse the ENG-10571 research brief's Podcast-name guidance when available, or always generate fresh?
* Per-campaign override vs strictly org-level (currently org-level only).

## Outcome

A persisted, reusable, editable podcast name with generate-and-confirm UX, so proven podcast copy ships with a real show name and is never asked twice.

AI_CONTEXT:
Ticket/PR: PR 2 — podcast-name capability. Blocked by ENG-10571.
Goal: capture/generate-and-confirm a podcast name once per workspace, persist org-level, reuse, edit; never block.
Non-goals: generation/prompt/model (ENG-10571); onboarding; hard-block.
Constraints: single org-level source of truth; partial mutation (no clobber); migration before deploy; no em-dashes in generated names; no AI-authorship mentions.
Code map: lib/db/schema/ai-sdr.ts (+migration), trpc/routers/ai-sdr.ts, lib/outreach/schemas/campaigns.ts, trpc/routers/outreach/campaigns.ts, lib/services/util.ts, lib/services/campaign-creator.ts, lib/inngest/functions/campaign/types.ts, lib/inngest/functions/campaign/process-campaign-creator.ts, schemas/submissions/cold-email-writer.ts, components/acquisition/cold-email-writer-form.tsx, hooks/campaign/use-campaign-wizard.ts, components/campaigns/new/campaign-wizard.tsx, types/campaign.ts, components/campaigns/new/steps/ (new).
Data context: read-only DB only if inspecting ai_sdr_setting rows; else code-only.
Feature flags: inherits ENG-10571's COLD_EMAIL_SONNET_RESEARCH_ENABLED.
Tests: allowlist threading; updatePodcastName trim/null/no-clobber/org-guard; generatePodcastName clean name + first-write-wins; schema round-trip; wizard reducer both entry points + back/refresh/duplicate-Next; onboarding unchanged.
QA: wizard podcast (empty + pre-set), standalone pre-fill/persist, generate-for-me, automated auto-persist.
Risks: allowlist silent-drop (util.ts:102); full-settings clobber; migration/deploy ordering (H13); wizard two-entry-point state-order (H14).
Review focus: every allowlist hop, partial-mutation tenancy, both wizard entry points, auto-persist race, onboarding untouched.

relatedSnapshot.title: RAINDROP ISSUE - improve fabrication details
relatedSnapshot.description:
Suggested title: Prevent AI SDR copywriter from fabricating names and podcast details

## Problem

AI SDR copy occasionally invents customer-facing details that are not supported by the knowledge base or conversation context. Examples include:

* Incorrect host names such as “Name 21 Name 22.”
* Internal campaign labels presented as podcast names, such as “Company Six.”
* Unsupported operational claims such as “the show is still in the early stages of launching.”

On August 17, `fabricated_detail` appeared in 17 terminal copy-review failures out of 1,531 reviewed runs: **1.11%**.

## Root cause

The generated context presents the campaign name as general campaign context without clearly identifying it as internal metadata. The copywriter can consequently reinterpret the label as a public-facing podcast or show name.

Additionally, when copy review rejects a response for `fabricated_detail`, the retry receives the generic review feedback but no targeted instructions explaining that unsupported details must be removed rather than renamed or replaced.

## Proposed change

Update the runtime-generated AI SDR context pack to:

* Mark campaign names as internal operational labels.
* Explicitly prohibit using campaign labels as podcast, show, event, company, product, or offer names unless supported by authoritative knowledge.
* Add targeted retry guidance for `fabricated_detail`.
* Instruct retries to remove unsupported people, titles, launch-status claims, and operational details.
* Prevent retries from replacing one unsupported detail with another plausible fabrication.
* Recommend generic phrasing or deferral when the required information is unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

* Internal campaign labels are clearly distinguished from customer-facing facts.
* A `fabricated_detail` rejection produces targeted grounding instructions on the next copywriter attempt.
* Retry guidance covers incorrect host names, podcast/show names, and unsupported launch or maturity claims.
* Unsupported details are removed or generalized rather than replaced.
* Regression tests cover the reported examples.
* Database-backed agent prompts are not modified.
* Booking, availability, slot offering, and rejected-slot logic are unchanged.

## Out of scope

* False booking-confirmation classification.
* Slot selection or alternative-slot generation.
* Reoffering previously rejected slots.
* Changes to active database agent submissions.
* Database schema or Inngest workflow changes.

relatedSnapshot.title: New AI SDR follow-up writer: Sonnet 5.5 on a follow-up-only prompt, switched on for all follow-ups
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Follow-up emails get written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 on a prompt built only for follow-ups, with the facts it needs. James decided on 6 Oct: Sonnet 5.5, switched on for **every** follow-up on day one. No gradual rollout and no A/B split. We measure the difference by comparing results before and after the switch.

In a blind test on 51 real quiet threads, Sonnet 5.5 with this prompt scored 8.0 out of 10, against 2.8 for today's follow-ups, at about $0.015 per email.

## Problem

* Today's follow-ups are generic "just checking in" notes. The writer uses the general reply prompt and knows nothing about the campaign, the sender or the prospect.
* In the blind test, today's follow-ups gave a clear next step in 1 of 51 cases and read like a template in almost all of them.

## User experience

* A prospect who went quiet gets a short email (20 to 60 words) in the same thread, from the same sender, that:
  * picks up on what they last said or asked;
  * gives one easy next step: point back to the times we offered that are still open, or ask "want me to send two times for next week?";
  * never invents times, links, episodes, prices or history.
* For threads that need a person (the prospect sent their own booking link, our earlier reply contradicts the campaign, a pricing deadlock), the AI sends nothing and creates a task for the deal owner instead.
* Live times come in the next ticket. Until then this writer offers no new times.

## What's included

1. **The new writer**, as a new arm in the writer setup from ENG-14757:
   * an agent row of type `followup-writer`, version 1;
   * model `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, effort **low**, no temperature, max output tokens 4000. Use exactly this. Medium effort was only tested with the older prompt, so don't switch to it;
   * the prompt is prompt v3, full text in the AI context. Copy it exactly.
2. **Fact sheet**, built by code for each follow-up (field list and sources in the AI context):
   * the cold email variant they received
   * our earlier emails as real text
   * their words
   * the campaign offer, method, niche and industry
   * show and host as written in this campaign's emails
   * sender first name, and the workspace's signature rule if it has one
   * title, company and company one-liner
   * today's date in the prospect's time zone
   * the situation and the step's job
   * which offered times are still open
   * allowed links
3. **Placeholders filled by code.** The model never types a time or a link:
   * `{{OFFERED_TIMES_OPEN}}` is replaced by the times we already offered that are still more than 2 hours away, in the prospect's time zone.
   * `{{LINK:id}}` is replaced by an allowed URL.
   * `{{TIMES}}` is not allowed yet. Treat it as a check failure.
4. **Code checks before send**, on every email from the new writer:
   * typed days, dates or times
   * raw URLs
   * banned phrases ("just checking in", "circling back" and the rest of the list)
   * false history ("thanks for getting back")
   * "the link I sent" when no link was sent
   * wrong sign-off name
   * leftover template text
   * over 80 words
   * a placeholder that could not be filled

   On failure, regenerate once with the reasons. If it fails again, skip this follow-up (`check_failed`). Never send, never escalate.
5. **Writer says "don't send"** (`send: false`): skip the follow-up (`writer_declined`) and create a CRM task for the deal owner with the reason.
6. **Subject line**: reuse the subject of our last sent email in the thread, never an out-of-office subject.
7. **Switch-on, in this order. Do not skip a step:**
   1. **Baseline.** ENG-14757 must have been live in production, with today's writer at 100%, for at least 14 full days. Those days are the "before" numbers. One week is not enough: results swing a lot from week to week. Its history fix and policy switches change today's results, so older data is not a fair baseline.
   2. **Gate.** Run the 51-case replay (AI context) in preview. All 51 must pass the code checks after at most one regeneration. Read 20 of the outputs yourself. Attach the pass/fail table and your notes to the PR. If either fails, fix before switching on.
   3. **Switch on.** In production, set the new writer's arm to weight 100 and today's writer (control) to weight 0. Leave control `active`: it is the instant rollback. Pausing the new arm sends every thread back to today's writer on its next follow-up, with no deploy.
   4. **Record the switch time.** Post the exact UTC timestamp as a comment on this ticket. The before/after report uses it.
   5. **First 3 days:** read 20 sent emails a day and post one line per day on this ticket ("20 read, 0 problems" or what you found).
8. **Measure.** Run the before/after report from ENG-14757 at 1, 2 and 4 weeks after the switch, and post the output on this ticket. Follow-ups rely on the code checks in this ticket. The ENG-14745 reply checker covers replies only (agreed 12 Oct 2026).

**Stop limits.** Pause the new arm (one database update) and tell James in Slack if any of these happen:

* "no" plus do-not-contact replies per follow-up sent run more than 2 points above the baseline rate, over at least 300 sends;
* any email goes to the wrong person or names the wrong sender, show or company;
* more than 15% of follow-ups are skipped by the checks;
* a mailbox gets a spam complaint traced to the new writer.

Also tell James (don't pause) if positive replies to follow-up 1 are more than 4 points below baseline after 1,000 sends.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14757: writer setup, logging, the history fix and the before/after report.

## Done when

- [ ] Replaying the 51 cases (fixture list in the AI context) in preview gives no email that fails the code checks after one regeneration, and the table plus 20 read emails are in the PR.
- [ ] No email from the new writer can contain a typed time, a raw URL, a banned phrase or a wrong sender name (code check and unit tests).
- [ ] `{{OFFERED_TIMES_OPEN}}` renders the correct still-open times in the prospect's time zone, and the email is skipped (not broken) when none are left.
- [ ] Writer-declined threads create a CRM task for the deal owner.
- [ ] Pausing the new arm in preview sends the next follow-up through today's writer (rollback tested).
- [ ] In production the new arm is at weight 100 and control at weight 0 (still active), after at least 14 days of baseline. The switch timestamp is posted on this ticket.
- [ ] Its `agent_executions` rows show the full fact sheet and v3 prompt.
- [ ] Three daily read-throughs and the 1, 2 and 4-week before/after reports are posted on this ticket.

## Implementation context

* Plan, bake-off results and prompt evolution: AI SDR Follow-ups v2
* Full prompt v3, fact-sheet fields with their sources, the check list, and the replay fixture list are in this ticket's AI context.md.
* The model decision comment of 6 Oct (Sonnet 5.5 only, 100%) replaces the earlier comment about Opus and Sonnet arms.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR follow-up invents a website URL for the podcast link a prospect requested
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Customer report (Intercom-sourced)**

**Intercom conversation**: <url:app.intercom.com>

**Conversation context**: Workspace owner reports that the AI SDR sent a prospect "a link to a website that is not associated with my company" when the prospect asked for the podcast link, and states the URL "was never provided to the AI SDR".

**Testable claim**: On an automated AI SDR follow-up, the generated email told the prospect "Here's the link you asked for: <url>", a URL that appears nowhere in the workspace knowledge base, resources, campaign configuration, or thread; the only source of that domain is the show name "Company Four" in the outreach copy.

**Evidence (production, 2026-09-14)**

* `scheduled_followup` row (sequence 2 of 4) status `sent`, executed 2026-09-14T15:06:31Z, message id <uuid>.
* `crm_message` (direction sent, source_provider Company One, `isManualReply: false`) body: "Just wanted to circle back on this. Here's the link you asked for: <url>".
* `ai_sdr_setting.resources = []` for the workspace; the knowledge base contains no URL; the campaign scripts payload contains only the show name, no domain.
* A human then corrected the thread (“I am sorry, I sent the wrong url”) after the automated email went out.

**Impact**: Fabricated URL sent to a prospect on an automated follow-up; this path does not run the copy-review fabrication guard used on reply emails.

**Unblock**: A human already corrected the thread. Workspace-side, the AI should not emit any podcast link until an approved link exists; adding the approved link to Resources would give the model a grounded source.

relatedSnapshot.title: AI SDR mishandles prospect "more info" requests
relatedSnapshot.description:
When prospects ask the AI SDR for more information, it does not explain the podcast offer or provide relevant details. Instead, it responds with confusing or incorrect statements (e.g. referencing being from the UK) and jumps straight to proposing call times without clarifying the context.

There are at least two affected conversations captured in Jam recordings:

* Screen recording 1
* Screen recording 2

The expectation is that when a prospect asks for more information, the AI SDR should prioritize clearly explaining the podcast (what it is, why they were invited, what to expect) before attempting to book a call.

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix emailScriptsMethod DB default from 'podcast' to null and backfill existing campaigns
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

The `emailScriptsMethod` column on `outreach__campaign` defaults to `'podcast'`. Any campaign where the type wasn't explicitly set (or was created before this field existed) silently becomes a podcast campaign, causing discovery/direct campaigns to be booked as pre-podcast calls.

## Current State

PR #2534 adds an AI-based campaign type detection step to the V2 workflow as a V2-scoped fix. However, the underlying DB default should also be corrected to prevent this class of bug from recurring in other codepaths.

## Proposed Fix

1. Change the DB column default from `'podcast'` to `null`
2. Update `getCallType` and any other consumers to handle `null` gracefully (already handles `undefined` → `discovery`)
3. Backfill existing campaigns that have `emailScriptsMethod = 'podcast'` but are actually discovery/direct campaigns

## Affected Workspaces

* Name 24 (<email>) - Company Eight
* Name 23 (<email>)

## References

* Related PR: <url:github.com>
* Schema: `lib/db/schema/outreach.ts` line 100-102
